subject: mathematics
question_text: If 2A and 3A are not odd multiples of π/2, prove that tan 3A · tan 2A · tan A = tan 3A − tan 2A − tan A.

verification.note: Source: Sri Chaitanya, FAST TRACK IPE for Jr. Students — Mathematics-IA (2026-27 edition), chapter 8 TRIGONOMETRIC RATIOS, Very Short Answer question 47(ii), book p.96. Only the question was taken. The solution, the step order and the mark split are this answer book's own work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S: the Mathematics-IA volume prints no per-step mark allocation on any answer. The 1 + 1 gives one mark to splitting 3A as 2A + A and writing the tan(A + B) formula, and one to clearing the denominator and separating the triple product from the three single tangents. The stem's condition was checked and is sufficient: if A itself were an odd multiple of π/2 then 3A would be one too, so ruling out 3A rules out A as well, and 1 − tan 2A tan A cannot be zero without tan 3A being undefined. Paper position: Maths-1A Section A prints ten very short answers of 2 marks each and the student writes all ten, under the 2026-27 pattern; Trigonometric Ratios and Transformations supplies two of those ten slots. This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

recall_prompt: Say how you would prove this — name how you split the angle and what you do with the denominator.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Write 3A = 2A + A and expand
steps.margin_note: First mark. 2A and 3A are not odd multiples of π/2, so tan 2A and tan 3A exist; and A cannot be one either, since 3A would then be one.
steps.memory_tip: 3A = 2A + A. The angle on the left is the sum of the two on the right, so the tan(A + B) formula fits straight away.
lines: 2A and 3A are not odd multiples of π/2,
so tan 2A and tan 3A exist. Nor is A one,
because 3A would then be one as well.

recall.must_convey: That 3A is written as 2A + A and the tan(A + B) formula is applied.
accept: split three A as two A plus A
apply the tan A plus B formula to two A and A
tan three A is tan two A plus tan A over one minus tan two A tan A
three A ni two A plus A ga split cheyyali
the angle on the left is the sum of the other two
heard_as: three A equals two A plus A
one minus tan two A tan A

steps.why: The two angles on the right, 2A and A, add to the angle on the left. Splitting 3A that way is the only step that brings all three tangents into a single equation, and everything after it is algebra.
common_mistakes: Using tan(2A − A) in place of tan(2A + A).
Writing the denominator as 1 + tan 2A tan A.

steps.label: Clear the denominator and rearrange
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Cross multiply, open the bracket, then put the triple product on one side and the three single tangents on the other.
steps.memory_tip: Cross multiply, open the bracket, then separate: triple product on one side, the three single tangents on the other.
lines: ⇒ tan3A − tan3A tan2A tanA = tan2A + tanA
tan3A − tan2A − tanA = tan3A tan2A tanA

recall.must_convey: That the denominator is cleared, the bracket opened, and the terms separated so the triple product equals the three single tangents.
accept: cross multiply and open the bracket
tan three A minus the triple product equals tan two A plus tan A
move the terms so the product is on one side
bracket open chesi terms ni separate cheyyali
the triple product equals tan three A minus tan two A minus tan A
reject: split three A as two A plus A

steps.why: Clearing the denominator is the whole of the second mark. Once the bracket is opened the triple product is already present with a minus sign, so a single rearrangement puts it alone on one side and the three single tangents on the other.
common_mistakes: Opening tan3A(1 − tan2A tanA) as tan3A − tan2A tanA.
Losing a sign when moving tan 2A and tan A across.
